subject_definitions:
<Subject 1>【茶娘】is the woman in <Picture 1>; her face, hair and identity strictly follow <Picture 1>. Her black hair is parted in the middle and gathered into a low bun fixed with a single light-wood hairpin, and she wears a fine gold necklace at her throat; she wears a plain off-white linen crossed-collar long robe with wide sleeves over a white inner dress, a pale-beige fabric sash tied at the waist with two long hanging ends, a very long flowing layered white skirt, and white flat cloth shoes. Her dance motion comes from <Video 1>. (character definition, never spoken aloud)
<Subject 2> is the Tujia courtyard in <Picture 1>: two-storey stilt houses of dark timber with grey tiled roofs and upturned eaves on both sides, grey flagstone paving with visible joints underfoot, a small leafy tree on the left, a blue-and-white porcelain lamp post on the right, red lanterns hanging under the eaves, and a low tea table with a few seated villagers far in the background, with open clear space at the center of the courtyard for the dancer.
<Subject 3> is the decoration on the fully opened skirt disc, visible only in the final part: an ivory-white linen circular ground with a thin pale-gold scalloped rim, a woven dark-red and black geometric brocade border running just inside the rim, two symmetrical ink-wash tea vines with palmate leaves and curling tendrils on the left and right, a central circular ink-wash painting of layered misty tea hills in light grey-green ink, and four large golden Chinese calligraphy characters 来凤藤茶 across the top center of the disc.
<Video 1> is the reference dance video: it provides the full seven-second temporal structure, the sleeve sweep into the turning body, the forward fold and the upward skirt flip, the skirt's flaring physics and timing, and the tripod-locked front-facing vertical framing.
<Video 2> is the grayscale depth-motion video extracted from <Video 1>: it guides only the figure's silhouette, the fold-and-turn path of the spine, and the circular expansion geometry of the skirt disc, and carries no color, face, costume or texture.
<Picture 1> is the character and scene reference image, showing the woman in a plain off-white linen robe standing in a Tujia stone courtyard with stilt houses and red lanterns behind her.

<Subject 3> (appears in the final part): attribute_transfer - the skirt disc keeps the reference layout of a thin scalloped rim, symmetrical side motifs, a central medallion and top-center characters, but the decoration is restyled as a plain ink-wash tea-and-vine design on ivory-white linen, and the only characters shown are the four golden characters defined in <Subject 3>.

detailed_description:
The target video is a cinematic, realistic live-action dance showcase in a vertical 9:16 frame, set in a Tujia stilt-house courtyard in soft overcast daylight; even white light falls from above, the red lanterns under the eaves give a low warm accent, and a few thin shadows of the eaves lie across the flagstones.
A single continuous tripod-locked full-body medium-long shot from start to finish, front-facing with the dancer centered, exactly as in <Video 1>; the framing never changes, with no cut, no second camera and no handheld movement; there is open space above her so the flared skirt can open into the frame.
Acting direction for the whole sequence: she is a real person quietly drawn into a dance rather than posing for the camera; her arms lead and her whole body weight drops into the fold. Nobody speaks, sings or narrates at any point; the sequence is carried only by movement, fabric and courtyard ambience.
The shot opens on <Subject 1> standing still in the middle of the courtyard, facing the camera, hands clasped low in front of her waist, as in <Picture 1>; the long white layered skirt rests on the flagstones around her feet.
She opens both wide sleeves outward and sweeps them up to shoulder height, twisting her upper body to one side; the linen robe and the long white skirt lift and swing out around her, the two beige sash ends fly outward, and the gold necklace and the wood hairpin sway with the turn.
Without breaking the turn she folds forward from the hips, drops her head toward the lower left of the frame, and sweeps both hands up so the long layered white skirt flips over her back.
Driven by the fold and the turn, the skirt whips upward and outward over her bent body and opens into a giant near-perfect circular disc facing the camera like a huge round paper fan; its plain underside flashes toward the lens for a moment, then the fabric keeps turning and settles with its decorated inner surface square to the camera.
The ivory-white disc fills most of the frame width and rotates gently into place as the motion settles: it is <Subject 3>, with two symmetrical ink-wash tea vines on the left and right, a central circular ink-wash painting of layered misty tea hills in light grey-green ink, a woven dark-red and black brocade border just inside the rim, and, across the top center of the disc, the four large golden Chinese calligraphy characters 来凤藤茶, laid out horizontally from left to right, evenly spaced, rendered clearly and correctly in this exact order, framed by the thin pale-gold scalloped rim.
Below the disc, <Subject 1> holds the fold, head tilted down, the wide sleeves and the beige sash hanging and trembling softly, her white cloth shoes planted on the flagstones; the huge ivory skirt disc holds its open shape above her with only soft fabric ripples until the final frame.
The camera stays perfectly still throughout; the stilt houses, the red lanterns and the far tea table remain in the background behind her, the daylight steady.
The frame contains no subtitles, no watermarks and no logos; the only legible Chinese characters are the four golden characters 来凤藤茶 on the opened skirt, rendered exactly as given, and every background surface carries no readable text.

overall_soundscape:
A quiet stone courtyard in daytime, with a soft breeze moving under the eaves, a few birds calling from the hillside, and faint chatter and clinking tea cups from the far table. Then the layered linen and cotton fabric gives a heavy airy whump and rustle as it swings up and flares open, settling into stillness as the disc opens.
